Large hail was reported by a CO-OP observer.
Thunderstorm wind gust to 60 mph was measured by the AWOS in Edinburg.
Thunderstorm winds gusting to 60 mph were reported by the U.S. Border Patrol.
Damaging thunderstorm winds knocked down trees, tore shingles off roofs, and snapped a power pole.
The forest service reported that three 12 inch diameter trees were snapped due to damaging winds from a severe thunderstorm.
Damage to mobile homes was reported by law enforcement in Mission.
A wind gust to 60 mph was measured by the ASOS in McAllen.
Damaging winds associated with a severe thunderstorm caused a roof collapse at a city maintenance facility. The roof fell on severeal vehicles.
Power lines were blown down on the west side of Edinburg by a thunderstorm wind gust.
Trees were reported down in Edinburg.
Several trees reported down in McAllen.
Skywarn spotter reported three ten-inch tree branches snapped off tree in yard.
Golf ball size hail reported by a spotter in Mission.

Mercedes police reported a weak tornado touched down briefly toppling two or three trees near Texas and Tenth Streets in the city. Numerous callers reported seeing a funnel cloud in the Mercedes area.

A microburst descending from a potent severe thunderstorm first produced damage just north of Alton, at a mobile home park near the intersection of Moorefield (Farm to Market Road 681) and Monte Cristo (Farm to Market Road 1925). In this neighborhood, at least six mobile homes we…
A strong thunderstorm produced a brief microburst from an outflow which was measured at 57 knots at Edinburg International Airport (KEBG).

A severe thunderstorm with a pronounced hail core rolled through the Donna-Alamo area during the mid morning, dropping large hail in several areas. Nickel size hail fell along the federal highway 83 expressway in Donna, shattering at least one automobile windshield. Penny size ha…

The Hidalgo County Fire Department reported marble to nickel size hail fell approximately 2 miles east of McCook on Farm to Market Road 681. The hail core intensified briefly as the parent thunderstorm moved east-southeast toward Highway 281.

A CO-OP observer in McCook reported heavy rainfall from a severe thunderstorms which produced wind gusts a little above 50 mph. A few minutes later, the same observer reported winds estimated near 60 mph, along with very heavy rainfall and frequent lightning.
A trained spotter reported nickel size hail fell in Donna during a thunderstorm that moved through Hidalgo County.

Quarter size hail fell along Milagros Road between Donna and Weslaco during a thunderstorm that moved through Hidalgo County. A news reporter from KRGV-TV-5 reported nickel size hail in the vicinity at around the same time.
A trained spotter reported that half-dollar size hail fell in Weslaco during a thunderstorm that moved through Hidalgo County.

Hidalgo County and McAllen City officials each reported penny size hail in southern Hidalgo County. The initial report, estimated around 225 PM CDT, was in the City of Hidalgo near the Rio Grande River; the second was near the McAllen/Miller Airport between 235 and 240 PM. The sa…
The Hidalgo County Emergency Manager reported penny to nickel size hail fell along East Wisconsin Road during another severe thunderstorm on June 1.
The public reported three quarters inch hail occurred during a rapidly developing thunderstorm during the early evening, just east of Weslaco.
A Hidalgo County official reported a roof blow off a small home at the intersection of 9 Mile Road and Moorefield Drive. Several Trees and power lines were down in the same area.

Channel 12 (McAllen Cable Access Television) reported quarter size and perhaps larger hail fell during a thunderstorm in the city of Mission during the evening. Nickel size hail was reported a bit earlier by a resident 1 mile north of Palmview, as well as several large limbs bein…

The public reported two separate wind gusts of 52 and 54 knots when a mini supercell raced south southeast through the Palmhurst/Mission/Sharyland area during the evening of June 3rd. The wind gusts knocked down numerous live oak and other trees and large limbs as the storm passe…
The public reported hail of approximately one inch in diameter continued falling as a severe thunderstorm raced through western Hidalgo County.
Wind Gust measured in the City of Mission.

Quarter sized hail was reported in Mission in two locations along or near Griffin Road (FM 495): At the intersection of Griffin and Glasscock, and just north of Griffin on Bryan Road. Events occurred between 755 PM and 803 PM CDT.
The public reported ping pong size hail fell across FM 490 east of Hargill.
The Hidalgo County Emergency Manager reported hail up to one and one half inches in diameter fell at the La Quinta Inn on south 10th Street during a thunderstorm which moved through the area.
Nickel sized hail was reported in San Carlos, 4 miles east of Edinburg.

Broadcast media reported a roof was blown off a mobile home during a thunderstorm that produced high winds across the area. Radar indicated a couplet of winds, as well as a reflectivity overhang, had moved across the area, suggesting a possible tornado. There were no confirmed re…

The Hidalgo County Emergency Manager reported strong winds occurred during a thunderstorm which knocked down some power lines in Weslaco. A funnel cloud was reported by the emergency manager approximately two miles west of Weslaco as the thunderstorm moved through the area. Peak …

A microburst tore through a colonia (migrant community) between Donna and Alamo, causing significant damage to mainly mobile homes and other unanchored structures. Two mobile homes were completely destroyed, and one under construction wood framed home collapsed. One outbuilding o…
NWS Student Volunteer (Oklahoma University) reported penny size hail near Edinburg.
Hail up to one inch in diameter fell south of Old 83 Highway south of Donna during a thunderstorm that moved through the Donna area in the afternoon.
Penny sized hail was reported in McAllen on Cynthia Street near the Wellness Center in the northeast portion of the city.
A local broadcast meteorologist reported a wind gust of 62 miles per hour during a strong pulse thunderstorm that affected Pharr.

A prolonged intense updraft was nearly stationary in the Donna-Alamo-San Juan area for nearly an hour, and at least two known quarter sized hail reports were received by the NWS office in Brownsville. The first occurred at 357 PM CST along Business Highway 83 in San Juan, reporte…

This short-lived tornado touched down in a subdivision approximately 4 miles east-northeast of the city of Hidalgo in southern Hidalgo County. Most of the damage in this area was limited to the overturning of trampolines, the knocking down of wooden privacy fences, an outdoor sto…

Frequent wind gusts, estimated at 70 to 75 mph, drove hail, some up to the size of baseballs, for more than an hour across portions of North McAllen, Mission, and Edinburg in Hidalgo County. Wind combined with hail resulted in numerous tree limbs blown down, defoliated trees, hom…

McAllen Miller Airport (KMFE) ASOS reported peak wind gusts at minimal hurricane force, 74 mph.
Trained Skywarn spotter reported quarter size hail in Pharr at the intersection of Hall Acres Road and Cage Boulevard.
Hidalgo County Sheriff's Office reported quarter to golfball size hail fell in the vicinity of McCook.
Golf ball to baseball size hail was reported over a swath of the heavily populated urban center of Mission and McAllen.
Reports of quarter to golf ball size hail were reported over a swath of heavily populated urban Mission and McAllen.
Public reported 60 mph wind gusts at Stewart and 21st in Mission. No damage was reported with the gusts.

Public reported softball size hail at McAllen High School. These hailstones, as well as golfball to baseball sized stones which fell for more than twenty minutes while traversing the McAllen/Mission/Pharr area, caused unknown damage to vehicles but little damage to other structur…

A semi trailer was blown over on US 281, 6 miles north of TX HWY 186. Driver of semi was injured. Driver stated that he had pulled onto the shoulder due to blinding rain and pelting hail and soon after, the downburst moved the trailer onto the dirt shoulder and then turned over. …

Between 9 and 945 PM, winds increased, rain poured down, and hail developed as the storm formed and began moving east. At approximately 930 PM, a microburst and large hail struck a colonia in Doolittle, damaging nearly every home (most were of poor construction) and rolling two u…
Several residents of a colonia in Doolittle reported at least five minutes of hail, up to the size of quarters, with a severe thunderstorm that also produced a damaging microburst in the area.
Public reported penny size hail 10 mile NE of Edinburg near Elsa at the intersection of FM2812 and Val Verde Road.

A supercell thunderstorm dropped hail the size of golfballs across a several mile swath of rural eastern Hidalgo County. The initial reports from the public indicated golf ball sized hail fell in Monte Alto at 615 pm CDT; radar reconcilation suggested the hail core drifted southw…

Estimated thunderstorm wind gusts of 65 to 70 mph, lifted a metal roof from a cinderblock shed at the residence of the brother of the Hidalgo County Emergency Manager, 3 miles north of Elsa. Debris from roof and building also injured livestock.

Public reported quarter to golf ball size hail at Monte Cristo and Filegonia Road in Elsa. Hail fell at approximately 630 PM, according to the report and radar reconciliation, and appears to have continued at quarter to golf-ball sized as the updraft redeveloped over and just sou…
Public reported quarter size hail at the intersection of Mile 12 and FM 491.

Internet report of a large-diameter tree blown down by thunderstorm winds near the intersection of North Victoria and Mile 10 Road, just north of Donna. Radar reconciliation suggest the winds fell just below severe limits.

An amateur radio operator in McAllen reported a carport had blown into adjacent building by thunderstorm winds. A nearby carport also damaged, all around the intersection of at Houston Street and 6th Avenue.
Broadcast media reported a tree blown down causing damage to a carport. Nearby KMFE ASOS reported a 42 kt wind gust.

At the Weslaco/Mid Valley Airport AWOS, a gust of 53 mph was recorded at 135 PM CDT. Further south, winds were estimated to be 60 to 65 mph based on the photos, descriptions, and prior experience with similar past events in the Rio Grande Valley. On the tarmac, the first damage o…

Mission police department reported several car ports damaged or destroyed in the 800 block of East 21st Street in Mission. ASOS at KMFE, about 5 miles to the SE, reported peak wind gust of 39 knots during the thunderstorm.

Four mobile homes, in poor condition and not anchored, were damaged in Doolittle near the intersection of Ingle Road and Doolittle Road. Two mobile homes lost tin roofs, one was moved off of its foundation, and one rolled over on its side. Estimated winds of 55 to 60 mph.

Media reported damage to a corrugated metal building, near the intersection of Inspiration Road and Highway 83 in Mission. At approximately the same time, one large limb weighing at least 100 pounds was blown off a mesquite tree nearby.

Local law enforcement had several reports of trees and powerlines down in Mission. The peak wind gust at McAllen/Miller Airport was 43 knots (48 mph) at 1935 CST, but from the multiple data reports it is assumed that pockets of wind reached 50 knots or higher in portions of Missi…

Several power poles down and power lines tangled in trees were reported throughout the city of Edinburg by the local fire department. Radar estimated potential wind gusts in excess of 50 knots (58 mph) from the bow echo within the squall line, which would imply such gusts in pock…
Local law enforcement reported signs blown down on Interstate 2 in Palmview.
Spotter reported wind gusts of an estimated 55 to 60 mph in Edcouch.
Two poorly constructed mobile homes were destroyed. One home had the roof removed and walls were collapsed.

Emergency manager reported two mobile homes with damage. One home had slid off the foundation and the second with part of roof torn off near the intersection of Mile 4 W and Mile 11 N road. Several tree limbs were knocked down onto power lines nearby along Mile 10 N road.
Dime to penny size hail was reported between Donna and Alamo.
Hidalgo County Sheriff's office reported several spots of trees and power lines down in and around Donna, Alamo, and San Juan.
A tree fell on a church near Lopezville and a mobile home had a roof overhang removed.
A tree, 8 inches in diameter, was uprooted in Pharr near the intersection of W. Bell and Dahlia, just south of Expressway 83 (IH-2).
Wind gusts of 60 to 65 mph removed a poorly anchored roof on a trailer home northwest of Alton and blew down some power lines and healthy large mesquite limbs.

Golf ball size hail reported near the intersection of Highway 107 and Stewart Road. Video from nearby locations indicated at least one cracked vehicle windshield; other photos showed mildly dented vehicles as well as some stripping of siding from one home.
Quarter size hail was reported near Alton.

Golf ball size hail was reported at the intersection of North Ware Road and Lark Street.
Quarter size hail reported at the intersection of Nolana and 23rd in north McAllen, and at the intersection of Savannah Avenue and 2nd Street (Col. Rowe Boulevard).
Trees were reported down at the intersection of Frontage Road and Bicentennial in McAllen. A nearby automated sensor at McAllen/Miller International Airport reported a 43 mph gust.

Microburst winds of 70 to 80 mph caused a large swath of damage across the Weslaco area. A newly constructed metal building had awning lifted, which helped tear off the front wall, the garage door was also blown in. Numerous softwood trees were blown down, some of which landed on…
Strong thunderstorm winds of 65 to 70 mph lifted a poorly anchored roof from a mobile home and moved a poorly constructed and poorly anchored mobile home off of its blocks.

The strong damaging winds damaged and destroyed many properties. A barn, made of aluminum and tin and built in the 1930s, was completely destroyed. A number of poorly constructed mobile homes, that were not tied down, and had no or poorly anchored roofs were destroyed and rendere…
Mercedes Police Department reported 10 to 12 power lines down and 15 to 20 trees down across the city of Mercedes.
Several powerlines were reported down in the city of Edcouch.
Public reported 60 acres of corn leveled by straight line winds at the corner of FM 493 and FM 2812.
Progresso Police Department reported a tree was blown down onto a vehicle at a residence on Watts Street in Progresso.

Hidalgo County EM reported widespread damage in La Villa. Multiple metal walls of a prefabricated building were peeled back and blown out 1 mile north of La Villa, a metal fence was blown down and metal canopies for recreational vehicles were blown off at Nature Resort RV Park in…
Mercedes Police Department reported a window blown out at the outlet mall and a palm tree blown down on Dawson Street.
Public reported a tree blown over in the city of Mission.
Palmview Police Department reported golf ball size hail near the intersection of La Homa Road and U.S. Highway 83.
Mission Police Department reported quarter size hail throughout much of the city of Mission.
Mission Police Department reported power lines and large tree branches down due to strong winds at the intersection of Inspiration and FM 495 and in the 1400 block of Doherty.

Estimated thunderstorm wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph knocked down trees and power lines across Pharr. The Pharr Police Department reported trees blown down at the intersection of Jackson and Ridge roads and on North Palm Road.
Estimated thunderstorm wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph knocked down trees and caused roof and antenna damage across the middle Rio Grande Valley, including the city of Weslaco.

The downburst winds tore the roof and at least one wall from a poorly constructed trailer at a colonia of Pueblo de Palmas, east of La Joya. In Alton, winds downed two trees, one of which fell onto a recreational vehicle. Five to seven power poles were downed or snapped in the sa…
Quarter size hail was reported by the public via Facebook near the intersection of Business 83 and 23rd Street in McAllen.
Fire Chief of Linn-San Manuel reported three power poles and lines down along FM 1017 and six trees were uprooted.

Damage began along Farm to Market Road 490 west of Hargill, where a string of three power poles were blown down, as well as several 1 to 3 inch diameter mesquite limbs. Crops in a nearby grain field were also blown at an angle from northwest to southeast. Damage was more notable …

Initial damage to tree limbs and some poorly built roofs in the Mission/Palmview area would intensify by the time the downburst reached the Madero and Granjeno communities, where more than 100 homes sustained varying levels of damage, dozens of power poles were felled, and hundre…
City of Pharr Emergency Manager reported golf ball size hail south of Pharr.
The ASOS at KMFE reported wind gust of 58 mph.

Hidalgo County Emergency Manager reported thunderstorm wind damage in the Las Canas subdivision (colonia). A roof was blown off a carport, a sheet of a tin roof was lifted on a mobile home and power lines were down. Homes in the neighborhood typically are very poorly built; other…
Public reported three quarter of an inch hail that lasted for 1 minute.
Public reported 1.5 inch hail near FM 2687 and Chihuahua in Zapata County.
McAllen Emergency Manager reported a tree down on Kennedy Avenue near 10th Street in McAllen. Time estimated by radar imagery and KMFE ASOS.

A gust of 53 mph was recorded at McAllen/Miller airport at 735 AM CST. At around the same time (735 AM), several power lines blown down in the south side of Pharr, just 2 to 4 miles east of the airport.

One large live oak tree was blown down at the Santa Ana National Wildlife Refuge along the Rio Grande, taking down several power lines and blocking an access road before removal. Another large tree was reported down a bit farther north in South Alamo, ten minutes later.

The pulse-severe thunderstorm that felled trees just north of the Rio Grande minutes earlier produced its strongest gusts in North Alamo. In and near the Red Barn Colonia, at least two poorly homes sustained full destruction, and several downed trees and fences were also reported…
Nickel-sized hail was reported via Facebook in the El Monte Colonia near Monte Alto during the pre-dawn hours of May 14, 2019.

The cooperative observer in McCook reported a measured wind gust to 58 mph, which blew down several large tree limbs and streen signs in the town, as well as blew down power lines four miles southeast of the town about four minutes later.

An off-duty NWS employee, along with local news media, reported a tractor trailer jack-knifed with the cab dangling on the side of Interstate 69C on the overpass above FM 490 just north of the South Texas International Airport. It was not determined if the jack-knife was caused b…

A large tree was blown down on the road near the Edinburg/McAllen line 5 miles southwest of Edinburg. Large branches were also blown down nearby. Peak wind gusts at McAllen/Miller International Airport reached 41 mph (36 knots) but reached 52 mph (45 knots) at South Texas Interna…

In addition to damaging winds that were surging through the area, the County Emergency Management staff reported estimated nickel-sized hail with the same severe thunderstorm in eastern Hidalgo County. Torrential, sideways-moving rain was also reported.
One tree was blown down along Cummings Road in Donna. Time estimated from radar and from nearby gust to 41 mph at McAllen/Miller Airport at 734 PM CDT.
Penny sized hail was reported in Alamo as a strong thunderstorm passed through just before sunset.
The daughter of a former NWS Brownsville/Rio Grande Valley employee reported quarter sized hail along N. 17th Street in McAllen.
Several portions of a fence were blown down at Chabad RGV in north McAllen.
Multiple power lines, poles, and trees were reported down with some blocking roads across Hidalgo county as the thunderstorm moved eastward across the county.
Several reports of quarter size hail east-northeast of mission.
Golf ball size hail reported to the northwest of McAllen via MPING report and a social media report.
The ASOS at MFE measured a wind gust of 61 mph as a thunderstorm moved through the area.

Residents impacted by the same pulse-severe storm that damaged nine homes in a colonia along the Hidalgo/Starr County line just northwest of Sullivan City reported a brief period of hail that accompanied the wind. Hail ranged from 1 inch to 1.75 inch (golfball size) in diameter.
Numerous reports on social media of trees damaged or uprooted near the Linn-San Manuel area.
Social media report of a damaged carport and a barn roof torn off in the Linn area. Time was estimated via radar.
As thunderstorms moved through the area, the RAWS site at Linn-San Manuel measured a wind gust to 60 mph or 52 knots.

As thunderstorms moved through the area, the ASOS station at the McAllen airport measured a gust to 63 mph, or 55 knots. Gusts of 54 knots or higher lasted for about 20 minutes, based on the station reports.

Numerous reports received via social media of tree damage and tree branches down on vehicles near Mercedes. Time was estimated via radar and based on NWS Storm Survey on damage from Donna to just east of Weslaco.
The AWOS at Edinburg International Airport measured a gust to 52 knots/60 mph as storms moved through the area during the early afternoon hours.
A Co-Op observer in McCook recorded a wind gust to 53 knots, or 61 mph. Hail between the size of peas and dimes was also noted at the time.
Power lines and crop damage (light to severe) were reported by the COOP observer in McCook. He also reported pea to nickel sized hail as the storms rolled through.
Additional pictures of tree damage was shared by the public near the intersection of Interstate 69C and Davis Road in Hidalgo County.

Social media reports of quarter to ping pong sized hail fell on the Palmview area in southwestern Hidalgo County around 4:22AM CDT on May 24th. There were additional areas of hail of pea to dime sized hail in La Joya and the Mission area around the same times.

A pulse-severe thunderstorm produced a microburst with winds estimated at 65 mph across the northeast side of Weslaco. Along its 2.3 mile track, damage included blown in siding at hangars at the airportand peeled back a metal roof on one of them. Other damage included a small out…

A member of the public shared pictures of hail up to 2 inches falling in the Peï¿½ï¿½itas area north of HWY 83.
A farmer reported hail up to 1.5 in diameter, which damaged his corn crop.
A CO-OP observer near McCook reported hail larger than golf balls (1.75), so went with an estimate near 2.
Member of the public reported quarter (1.0) sized hail in the Alton area.
Several members of the public reported ping pong ball (1.5) sized hail in and around the Palmview area.

Multiple reports of golf ball (1.75) to baseball (2.75) size hail falling across the Peï¿½ï¿½itas area. Several pictures showed hail sizes up to baseballs, with a few pictures showing hail damaged car windshields. One picture in particular showed hail going through the rear winds…

Member of the public shared pictures of golf ball (1.75) hail in and around the Peï¿½ï¿½itas area.
The McAllen Emergency Operations Center reported half dollar (1.25) sized hail in McAllen.

The ASOS station at McAllen-Miller International Airport (KMFE) recorded a wind gust of 62 mph at 4:40PM CDT the afternoon of April 21st. There was also some damage to a warehouse a few miles south of the airport with a garage door blown inward.
Multiple reports from the public of small marble (0.5) to half dollar (1.25) sized hail in and around McAllen.
Public reported quarter (1.0) sized hail covering the yard with the largest stones estimated to be tennis ball (2.5) sized in the Mission area.

A member of the public shared a picture of a warehouse garage door blown in by a thunderstorm wind gust. Timing estimated by radar and wind gust estimated by using the McAllen-Miller International Airport ASOS, which recorded a gust to 54 knots.

Members of the public reported large tree limbs knocked down along Ware Road in McAllen. Timing estimated by radar and wind gust estimated by using the McAllen-Miller International Airport (KMFE) ASOS.
Member of the public reported half dollar (1.25) sized hail in and around the Donna area.
The McAllen-Miller International Airport (KMFE) ASOS recorded a wind gust of 59 knots, or 68 mph, at 1:02PM CDT.
Video shared by a member of the public shows several large trees down along El Pinto Road near Rosendo Benavides Elementary School. Time estimated by radar.
Member of the publics shows several mesquite trees down along Garza Avenue north of Military road. Time estimated by radar.
Video from the public shows the metal roof of a carport peeled back near the intersection of Mile 3 Road and Tom Gill Road. Time estimated by radar.

A member of the public shared pictures with an NWS employee of significant damage to a mobile home trailer. The pictures show the mobile home destroyed with only one wall still standing. Timing estimated by radar.

A member of the public shared pictures of the Burger King in Palmview with its windows blown out around the play area. It's located at the intersection of Frontage Road and La Homa Road. Timing estimated from radar.
Broadcast media shared a picture of a few food trucks and trailers flipped over near the intersection of Bryan Road and Business 83 near Mission City Hall. Time estimated by radar.

Weslaco Fire Marshal reported damage to four to five trees in his neighborhood in Mission.
Member of the public called in to report several trees that were uprooted along with several others that lost tree limbs. Timing based on their report and radar.
Several citizens reported several large trees and traffic signs down along with stop signs pulled out of the ground along Highway 495 and Sugar Road. Timing estimated by radar.

A member of the public called to report dime and nickel sized hail. Time estimated on the time of the call and radar.
